what_it_usually_means: The portal could not find your institution in its list, often because the name is written differently, the school has not yet submitted records for the current cycle, or there is a temporary lookup issue.
what_to_do: Confirm you are searching with the exact official name of your institution.
Try alternative spellings or the short form if the portal offers search suggestions.
Check whether your institution has publicly announced that it has submitted student data to NELFUND for this cycle.
Contact your institution's student affairs or NELFUND liaison office for confirmation.
Return to the official portal after any update from your institution rather than using unofficial workarounds.
avoid_this: Do not use unofficial websites or paid agents claiming they can force your school to appear.
Do not repeatedly resubmit the same search expecting a different result without trying the steps above.
still_stuck: If your school still does not appear after trying the steps above, contact the official NELFUND channels listed on nelf.gov.ng and your institution's NELFUND liaison.

what_it_usually_means: Pending usually means your application is still moving through verification stages (identity, JAMB, institutional, bank). It is not a final decision.
what_to_do: Check the status page on the official portal regularly for any stage-specific message.
Ensure your NIN, JAMB, and bank details are consistent across records.
Wait for institutional verification if that stage is still open. Your school may still be processing submissions.
Contact official NELFUND support only after a reasonable waiting period and if the portal itself suggests next steps.
avoid_this: Do not submit multiple duplicate applications out of anxiety.
Do not pay anyone claiming they can speed up approval.
still_stuck: Use the official portal contact channels and your institution's student affairs office. Keep screenshots of your status page.

what_it_usually_means: Rejection is usually tied to a specific verification failure (identity mismatch, institutional record, eligibility, or incomplete information). The portal should surface a reason. This guide cannot invent your personal rejection reason.
what_to_do: Read the exact rejection or failure message on the official portal.
Compare your NIN, JAMB, name spelling, date of birth, and matriculation number against official documents.
Correct any mismatch and re-apply only if the portal allows a new or corrected submission.
If the reason is institutional, contact your school's NELFUND liaison.
avoid_this: Do not assume the reason without checking the portal message.
Do not pay third parties claiming they can reverse a rejection.
still_stuck: Escalate through official NELFUND support channels listed on nelf.gov.ng after documenting the portal message and the corrections you already made.

problem: I already paid my school fees
what_it_usually_means: You paid institutional charges before NELFUND disbursement. How refunds or credits work depends on both NELFUND rules and your institution's own procedures.
what_to_do: Check the official portal for any guidance on fees already paid.
Contact your institution's bursary or NELFUND liaison for their refund/credit process.
Keep receipts and proof of payment.
Do not assume a nationwide refund rule applies to every school.
avoid_this: Do not rely on social media claims about automatic refunds.
Do not ignore your institution's specific instructions.
still_stuck: Your institution's student portal and the office handling NELFUND coordination are the practical next steps.

what_it_usually_means: The portal could not match your personal or academic details to an institutional record.
what_to_do: Re-check NIN, JAMB number, name spelling, and matriculation number against official documents.
Confirm with your institution that your student record has been submitted to NELFUND.
Try again after any update from your school.
avoid_this: Do not invent or alter details to force a match.
Do not use unofficial tools claiming to fix the lookup.
still_stuck: Contact your institution's NELFUND liaison and official NELFUND support with evidence of your records.

what_it_usually_means: Upkeep is the monthly living allowance component of the NELFUND loan (currently confirmed at ₦20,000 per month). It is paid to your bank account when approved, and it must be repaid as part of the loan.
what_to_do: Read the upkeep page on this guide for the confirmed amount and the loan nature of the funding.
Decide whether you need upkeep in addition to institutional charges before selecting it on the portal.
Confirm current figures on the official portal before budgeting.
avoid_this: Do not treat upkeep as free money.
Do not rely on unofficial figures such as ₦25,000 unless an official source confirms a change.
still_stuck: Use the official portal and the Sources page on this guide for primary confirmation.

what_it_usually_means: OOU-specific record matching or upload timing may be involved in addition to the general NELFUND lookup.
what_to_do: Confirm your matriculation number matches the OOU student portal exactly.
Ask the OOU office responsible for NELFUND coordination whether records for your session have been submitted.
Follow any OOU student portal notices about NELFUND.
avoid_this: Do not assume a process from another university applies at OOU.
still_stuck: Contact the OOU office handling NELFUND liaison and keep evidence of your portal attempts.
